enriched_description: Snakelike fish measuring 30-300 cm with elongated cylindrical body. Skin smooth and slimy with scaleless surface in brown, green, black, or yellow coloration. Head small with elongated jaws bearing sharp teeth. Eyes small and covered with skin in some species. Dorsal, caudal, and anal fins continuous forming single vertical fin margin. No ventral (pelvic) fins. Pectoral fins small or absent. Gills reduced to small pores. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Voracious marine or freshwater fish with catadromous or anadromous migration.

Salmonid fish measuring 50-80 cm weighing 2-7 kg. Body streamlined and laterally compressed. Scales small and silvery with blue-green dorsal coloration and silver sides. Spots on back and upper lobe of tail. Head pointed with hooked jaw (kype) in spawning males. Eyes large. Mouth terminal. Dorsal fin single with adipose fin posterior. Tail deeply forked. Breeding males develop red body coloration with green head. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Small salmon of northern Pacific coasts and Great Lakes.

Butterflyfish measuring 15-25 cm with laterally compressed disc-shaped body. Coloration striking gold and black: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin. Dorsal fin continuous with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions. Anal fin similar. Tail rounded. Mouth small and protrusible with brush-like teeth. Eyes large. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Marine reef fish of West Indies to Brazil with bright aposematic coloration.

Damselfish measuring 5-15 cm with laterally compressed oval body. Coloration variable by species: orange, red, yellow, or black with distinctive white bars or stripes. Body covered with small ctenoid scales. Dorsal fin continuous with 10-17 spines. Anal fin with 2 spines. Tail rounded or slightly emarginate. Eyes large. Mouth small. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Lives in symbiotic association with sea anemones, protected by mucus coating. Sequential hermaphroditism.

Large primitive fish measuring 100-300 cm weighing 15-400 kg. Body elongated and fusiform with five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales. Coloration gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface. Head elongated with protrusible mouth on ventral surface. Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth. Tail heterocercal (asymmetrical). Snout pointed. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Large primitive fish valued for flesh and caviar roe.

Primitive fish measuring 60-300 cm with elongated cylindrical body. Body covered with hard ganoid scales (diamond-shaped enamel-coated plates) providing armor-like protection. Coloration olive-brown to gray. Head elongated with long alligator-like jaws bearing needlelike sharp teeth. Eyes positioned dorsally. Dorsal and anal fins positioned far posterior near tail. Tail rounded (not forked). Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Predaceous North American freshwater fish with dual respiration capability.

Scorpaenid fish measuring 25-40 cm with laterally compressed body. Coloration brightly striped in red, white, brown, or black bands. Dorsal fin with 13 elongated venomous spines that fan outward like mane. Pectoral fins large and fan-like with elongated rays. Pelvic fins also with elongated spines. Head large with prominent eyes and wide mouth. Body covered with small scales. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Venomous spines deliver painful sting. Tropical Pacific reef fish.

Plectognath fish measuring 10-60 cm with elongated spiny body capable of inflation. Body covered with small spines or smooth skin in variable coloration including brown, gray, yellow, or patterned. Eyes large and positioned high on head. Mouth small with beak-like fused teeth (four teeth forming two plates). Dorsal and anal fins small and positioned posteriorly. No pelvic fins. Tail rounded. When threatened, inflates body by swallowing water or air to form spherical shape. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, vertebral column, and gill respiration. Contains potent tetrodotoxin neurotoxin.

Manual calculating device consisting of rectangular wooden or metal frame with parallel rods or wires. Each rod holds multiple sliding beads (typically 5-7 per rod) made of wood, plastic, or stone. Beads divided into two sections by horizontal reckoning bar: upper deck (heaven beads, value 5) and lower deck (earth beads, value 1). Frame dimensions approximately 20-30 cm wide by 10-15 cm tall. Beads slide smoothly along rods for arithmetic operations. Geometric structure: rectangular frame with uniform rod spacing. Material: wood, bamboo, or metal construction.

Traditional garment consisting of loose black robe extending from head to toe. Fabric: lightweight black crepe, chiffon, or georgette material with matte finish. Cut: full-length flowing silhouette with wide sleeves extending to wrists. Neckline: open front or closed with concealed closure. Length: floor-length (140-160 cm). Width: generous drape allowing full body coverage. Some variants feature embroidery, beading, or embellishment along edges. Geometric structure: rectangular draped form with minimal tailoring. Worn over regular clothing as outer garment.
